findings.title: Only additions are tracked, so new deletions and reverted deletions are missed
findings.why: `now` and `before` are built with `_added`, and removals in `between` are only considered when they overlap `before`. A later commit that deletes a pristine base line (or file) has no `hunk.added` and no `before` overlap, so it is dropped; a later commit that re-adds a line the PR had deleted has an added line not in `now` and no removal, so it is also dropped. The increment can be empty even though the PR's own diff changed.

findings.title: Take-back is skipped when the same hunk also has kept additions
findings.why: The `elif` only checks `hunk.removed` when `kept` is empty. With `-U0`, a deletion of a PR-added line adjacent to another PR change lands in the same hunk; `kept` is non-empty, so the reverted line is never added to `lines`. The later round will not review that reverted line.

findings.title: Took-back branch can emit a head-side path/line absent from head
findings.why: For a file deleted in head (or a file emptied by the deletion), `hunk.new_path` is still the diff header's old path and `at` is forced to at least 1. The code then records a head-side line for a file/line that does not exist, breaking the `Increment` contract and causing downstream comment placement to fail or target the wrong place.

findings.title: Diff header parsing fails on quoted paths and paths containing ' b/'
findings.why: `core.quotePath=false` only disables octal quoting; git still C-quotes paths with quotes, backslashes, tabs, or newlines, which `_FILE` does not match. The greedy `(.+) b/(.+)` also misparses a path containing the substring ' b/'. When `_FILE` does not match, `_hunks` keeps the previous file's paths and attributes the following hunks to the wrong file.

findings.title: All Git errors are treated as an unknown previous head
findings.why: The `try` covers diffs for the current `base...head` and `previous_head..head` as well as the previous-head existence check. A missing/corrupt current base or head, a timeout, or any other `GitError` returns `None` (full review), masking the real failure and violating the documented condition that `None` means the previous head is unknown.
